q: 'Free time' for loading/unloading of wagons is prescribed to?

options.A: Define the detention period after which demurrage accrues
options.D: Limit the station's working hours

q: Stabling charges are levied on?

options.B: Wagons stabled at a station at the owner's request beyond free time
options.D: Goods stored in the station master's office

q: For goods lost in transit, compensation is normally payable to?

options.C: The person entitled under the railway receipt, usually the consignee
options.D: The state government

q: A 'damage and deficiency' message is raised by the destination station to?

options.D: Inform the booking station and claims office of loss or damage noticed

q: Goods of a dangerous or hazardous nature are accepted for carriage only if?

options.A: They are packed and declared per the rules for dangerous goods
options.C: They move only by passenger train
options.D: The station master personally escorts them

q: 'Open delivery' of a consignment is granted when?

options.B: The consignee suspects damage and wants assessment before taking delivery
options.D: The wagon is overloaded

q: Assessment of damage during open delivery is done by?

options.C: Railway staff with the consignee, recording the extent of damage
options.D: The insurance company only

q: If the consignee refuses to take delivery, the railway may?

options.A: Abandon the goods on the platform
options.B: Send them back free of charge
options.D: Store them, levy wharfage/demurrage, and ultimately dispose of them per rules

q: 'Undercharges' detected in goods accounts refer to?

options.A: Short collection of freight or charges due to wrong rate or weight
options.C: Theft of cash at the station
options.D: Demurrage waived by the DRM

q: 'Overcharges' in goods traffic are refunded to the claimant after?

options.A: Verbal request at the goods shed
options.B: A written claim with the railway receipt, verified against the tariff
options.D: A court decree in every case

q: The Goods Tariff is revised periodically mainly to?

options.C: Reflect costs, policy, and market conditions in freight rates
options.D: Eliminate minimum weight conditions

q: Classification of commodities in the Goods Tariff is based on?

options.D: Value, density, risk, and handling characteristics

q: A higher class rate applies to a commodity generally when it is?

options.A: High-valued, light, or risky to carry
options.D: Booked in trainloads

q: 'Smalls' (small consignments) are normally charged?

options.B: At the smalls rate which is higher per unit than wagonload rates
options.D: At half the wagonload rate

q: In station goods accounts, cash collected is remitted to the bank/cash office with?

options.C: A remittance advice linking collections to the returns
options.D: The guard's signature

q: Outstanding freight dues from a regular consignor are watched through?

options.D: The sundry debtors/credit note records of the station

q: Waiver of demurrage or wharfage is granted by?

options.A: The competent authority under delegated powers for genuine hardship
options.D: No one; waiver is never allowed

q: Claims for compensation are settled and paid through?

options.B: The claims office after verification, by cheque or bank transfer
options.D: The consignor's agent without documents

q: The primary audit check on goods earnings at stations focuses on?

options.C: Correct application of tariff rates, weights, and completeness of collections
options.D: Staff uniform compliance

q: Monthly goods earnings returns from stations are used by the accounts department to?

options.D: Compile zonal earnings, reconcile remittances, and detect undercharges

q: What is a Railway Receipt (RR)?

options.A: The document of title issued when goods are accepted for carriage
options.B: A free travel pass for use in goods trains
options.C: A monthly summary of wagon loadings at a station
options.D: A licence for operating a private siding

q: Freight for a consignment is normally computed on:

options.A: The distance multiplied by the wagon tare weight
options.B: The cubic capacity of the wagon used
options.C: The declared value of the goods
options.D: The chargeable weight multiplied by the applicable rate

q: The term 'chargeable weight' means:

options.A: The maximum axle load permitted for the wagon
options.B: The payload weight after deducting the wagon tare
options.C: The weight of the empty wagon
options.D: The weight on which freight is levied, subject to prescribed minimum conditions

q: Which document travels with the goods as the record of the contract of carriage?

options.D: Credit note

q: 'To-pay' traffic means freight is:

options.A: Collected at the destination station before delivery of goods
options.B: Written off as irrecoverable by the railway
options.C: Borne by the railway department concerned
options.D: Prepaid by the consignor at the booking station

q: Demurrage charges are levied for:

options.A: Late payment of freight bills by customers
options.B: Detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed
options.D: Damage caused to railway property

q: Wharfage is a charge levied for:

options.A: Transhipment of goods between different gauges
options.B: Use of railway land by private parties
options.C: Detention of goods on railway premises beyond the free time
options.D: Weighment of consignments at weighbridges

q: Siding charges are recovered from:

options.C: All consignors at a uniform rate
options.D: Owners or users of private sidings for engine, staff and related services

q: The Traffic Accounts Office in a zonal railway is primarily responsible for:

options.C: Operating goods trains in the zone
options.D: Compiling traffic earnings and preparing accounts returns

q: Station freight earnings reach the Traffic Accounts Office through:

options.A: Monthly station returns of goods earnings
options.C: Wagon census data from operating staff
options.D: Daily cash summaries sent by station masters

q: In railway accounts, 'earnings' represent:

options.B: Revenue credited to the revenue account after admissible adjustments
options.C: Budget estimates of revenue for the year
options.D: Cash collected at stations during the month

q: Station outstanding statements are important because they show:

options.B: The number of staff posted at a station
options.C: Amounts earned but not yet realised or remitted by stations
options.D: Fuel consumed by locomotives during the month

q: A suspense head in traffic accounts is used to:

options.C: Hold amounts temporarily pending final allocation or clearance
options.D: Record capital expenditure on new lines

q: Freight realised but not yet allocated to final heads is parked in:

options.D: The provident fund account

q: Reconciling wagons loaded with RRs issued ensures that:

options.A: Staff attendance at the station is complete
options.B: Wagon hire charges are correctly fixed
options.D: Every loaded wagon is backed by a valid receipt

q: An 'unconnected wagon' is one that:

options.B: Arrives at destination without a corresponding waybill or RR
options.C: Is under repair in the workshop
options.D: Has been returned empty to the home station

q: Monthly freight returns enable the zone to:

options.A: Prepare crew rosters for the next month
options.B: Compile its goods earnings for the month for accounts purposes
options.D: Plan wagon procurement for the year

q: A monthly goods earnings return normally consolidates:

options.B: Passenger ticket sales at the station
options.C: Freight collected, rebates allowed, refunds paid and outstandings
options.D: Staff payroll data for the month

q: 'Through traffic' in freight accounting refers to consignments:

options.A: Carried free of charge for railway use
options.D: Moving over more than one railway, requiring apportionment of earnings

q: Through-traffic freight earnings are shared between railways:

options.A: Under apportionment rules based on the carriage performed by each railway
options.B: With the originating railway retaining the whole amount
options.C: With the destination railway retaining the whole amount
options.D: By equal division between the railways

q: 'Short credit' at a goods station means:

options.A: Freight charged below the published rate
options.B: Wagons loaded below their carrying capacity
options.C: Rebates paid in excess of the claim
options.D: Earnings collected but remitted short of the amount due

q: 'Excess credit' reported by a station would require:

options.B: Investigation and refund or adjustment to the party concerned
options.D: Suspension of the station master

q: RR reconciliation with wagon loading records helps detect:

options.D: Incorrect timetable planning

q: A wagon shown as loaded but missing from station returns indicates:

options.D: Possible leakage of freight revenue

q: 'RRs issued but not accounted' are treated as:

options.D: Outstanding items requiring early clearance

q: Reconciliation statements of freight traffic are prepared by:

options.A: The Traffic Accounts Office from station returns and operating data
options.B: The locomotive crew after each trip
options.D: The station master alone

q: Wagon numbers on RRs and waybills are cross-checked to:

options.B: Prevent misuse of railway wagons for unbooked traffic
options.D: Allot priority in train formation

q: Delays in RR reconciliation can lead to:

options.D: Reduction in wagon detention

q: Freight suspense balances must be:

options.A: Written off at the end of each month
options.C: Cleared promptly and not allowed to accumulate
options.D: Transferred to the capital account yearly

q: Outstanding 'to-pay' freight at destination is shown as:

options.A: A capital receipt in the accounts
options.B: An advance paid to the consignor
options.D: Station outstanding until collected or written off under rules

q: Unrealised freight outstanding beyond the prescribed period is:

options.A: Reported for recovery action or write-off sanction
options.D: Automatically written off

q: 'Departmental traffic' refers to:

options.B: The railway's own materials carried for departmental use
options.D: Containers carried for private operators

q: Freight on departmental traffic is:

options.A: Charged at full public rates in cash
options.B: Accounted separately and charged to the consuming department
options.C: Written off as a social obligation
options.D: Collected from the consignor in advance

q: Public traffic differs from departmental traffic in that:

options.B: It is carried free of charge
options.C: It is carried for outside parties at published rates
options.D: It needs no documentation

q: Stores moved for railway use are generally carried:

options.D: At departmental rates or under departmental account

q: Ballast and permanent-way materials moved departmentally are debited to:

options.A: The engineering department's revenue or works heads
options.D: The passenger earnings account

q: Departmental traffic must still be:

options.A: Documented with RRs or waybills for accounting control
options.C: Reported to the Railway Board daily
options.D: Exempt from all records

q: Misclassifying public traffic as departmental results in:

options.B: Loss of freight revenue to the railway
options.D: Better customer relations

q: Military traffic is carried on the basis of:

options.B: Cash payment at the booking counter
options.C: Military credit notes raised against defence authorities
options.D: Free passes issued to units

q: Freight bills for military traffic are preferred to:

options.D: The defence accounts authorities for payment

q: Military traffic accounting is kept separate to:

options.A: Hide the volume of defence movement
options.B: Reduce the work of the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: Facilitate recovery of dues from the defence services

q: Unpaid military credit notes appear in accounts as:

options.D: Outstanding freight dues recoverable from defence

q: A city booking agency:

options.B: Accepts goods bookings in a city on behalf of the railway
options.D: Supplies catering on goods trains

q: Out-agencies are established at places:

options.C: Not served directly by rail, to collect and deliver goods
options.D: Inside railway workshops

q: City booking and out-agencies are remunerated through:

options.B: Fixed monthly salaries from the railway
options.C: Commission on the traffic handled by them
options.D: A share in wagon hire charges

q: Remittances received from booking agencies must be:

options.D: Reconciled with the traffic booked through them

q: Container traffic on Indian Railways is mainly handled through:

options.A: CONCOR under a haulage arrangement with the railways
options.D: Departmental wagon pools

q: The railway's earning from container traffic mainly takes the form of:

options.B: Haulage charges for moving the containers
options.D: Customs duty collected at ports

q: Empty container movement is accounted for:

options.A: As free traffic with no records
options.B: Under the agreed haulage terms between the railway and the operator
options.D: Only in the annual statistical report

q: Container terminal reporting is needed for:

options.C: Correct assessment and billing of haulage charges
options.D: Fixing passenger train timings

q: CONCOR interface accounting covers:

options.D: Haulage bills, terminal charges and their reconciliation

q: Penal charges for overloading of wagons are credited to:

options.D: The staff benevolent fund

q: Weighment of loaded wagons is required to:

options.A: Verify declared weight and detect overloading
options.D: Fix the colour of the wagon

q: Freight rebate schemes are intended to:

options.B: Encourage higher or assured traffic volumes
options.C: Reduce the number of goods customers
options.D: Eliminate departmental traffic

q: A freight rebate is generally:

options.B: A surcharge over the published rate
options.C: A concession on published rates subject to fulfilment of conditions
options.D: A cash advance to the customer

q: Rebate claims of customers must be:

options.A: Rejected as a matter of policy
options.D: Verified against the scheme conditions before payment

q: Assured-volume or round-trip rebate schemes aim to:

options.D: Improve wagon utilisation and secure traffic

q: Incorrect rebate payments detected later are recovered through:

options.A: Debit against the party or adjustment in the accounts
options.D: Write-off without enquiry

q: Rebate payments must be accounted:

options.B: Net of earnings, with proper scheme-wise records
options.D: Only in the annual report

q: The Traffic Accounts Office verifies rebate claims using:

options.C: Station returns, RR data and scheme documentation
options.D: Newspaper reports on freight trends
